data.title: Amino Acid Sensing by mTORC1: Intracellular Transporters Mark the Spot
data.authors: Goberdhan DC; Wilson C; Harris AL

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Review: intracellular amino-acid transporters mark the site of mTORC1 activation.
data.abstract_excerpt: Cell metabolism and growth are matched to nutrient availability via the amino-acid-regulated mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1). Transporters have emerged as important amino acid sensors controlling mTOR recruitment and activation at the surface of multiple intracellular compartments. Classically, this has involved late endosomes and lysosomes, but now, in a recent twist, also the Golgi apparatus. Here we propose a model in which specific amino acids in assorted compartments activate different mTORC1 complexes, which may have distinct drug sensitivities and functions.
